Build a 12-second countdown leader in this empty comp. **The ring** A circular sweep ring, centred, drawn as a stroked circle rather than a filled disc, that empties clockwise over ten seconds — a full ring at 0s, nothing left at 10s. Around the outside of it a thinner ring rotates slowly for the whole twelve seconds with heavy motion blur, so it reads as spinning rather than stepping. Two thin crosshair lines run edge to edge through the centre. **The count** Inside the ring, a counter counts down 10, 9, 8 … 1, one number per second, each landing hard rather than fading in. The numbers start hidden behind a wipe that sweeps up from the bottom across the first second. That wipe is a reveal, not part of the design: once it has done its job it should be gone. The ring wants a soft feathered edge the whole way through, so if you mask it, that mask has to survive the wipe being removed. Tick marks sit around the ring at each second. **Everything else** - The background is deep warm charcoal with a subtle radial falloff, deepest at the corners. - A marker on each second boundary, its comment giving the number. - The last two seconds accelerate: the ring's sweep and the ticks speed up so the count lands hard on zero. - One frame of white flash over the whole frame at the end. I would like that ring's stroke drawn with a two-colour gradient. If that is out of reach, say so and use the closest thing that is honest rather than approximating it quietly. **The timeline I am asking for** - 0s — the ring is full, the counter is hidden, the wipe starts sweeping up. - 0–1s — the wipe reveals the counter, then the wipe is gone. - 0–9s — the counter reads 10, 9, 8 … 1, one number a second. - 8–10s — the ring's sweep and the ticks accelerate. - 10s — the sweep reaches nothing, and the count lands hard on zero. - 10s — one frame of white flash over the whole frame. - 10–12s — the finished frame holds; the outer ring keeps spinning to the end. **One thing I want driven deliberately** The spinning outer ring should be driven by a parent null rather than keyframed directly, and I want the ring's position stated explicitly rather than left wherever it lands. Whichever order you write those two in, if After Effects moves that value when the parenting lands, write the position it actually ends up holding and tell me exactly what it did to it rather than quietly correcting it. Tell me at the end how many Undos it takes to take the whole thing back.
